frozen_candidate_root_contribution: Across the dispositional derivational family (~327 of 339 occ.: verb, raḥmah, raḥīm, al-Raḥmān, rāḥimīn, arḥam, ruḥm, ruḥamāʾ, marḥamah) rHm contributes a BENEFICENT SPARING FAVOR extended by a superior/agent toward one in need or weakness — inclining to spare from harm/punishment and to bestow benefit. It is relational and directional (God→creature, or strong→weak), enacted rather than merely felt (instantiated as deliverance, reviving rain, provision, revelation, the Prophet, reward), discretionary/contingent (bestowed man yashāʾ, conditioned on taqwā), and defined by the corpus as the pole OPPOSITE to punishment (ʿadhāb) and distinct from forgiveness (maghfira). This account is NOT extended to the concrete nominal arḥām (womb/blood-kinship, 12 occ.), which the Qurʾan never bridges to the disposition.

internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Almost the whole root (327/339 occurrences) means one thing: a stronger party — nearly always God — showing mercy, i.e. sparing someone from harm or punishment and giving them good. The Qurʾan shows this by opposing mercy to punishment (29:21, 17:54), by making 'mercy' a concrete gift (rescue, rain, the Book, the Prophet, paradise), and by always asking for mercy alongside — but separately from — forgiveness. 'al-Raḥmān' is this same mercy turned into a reserved name of God, while 'raḥīm' is a shareable attribute that can even describe the Prophet (9:128); the Qurʾan itself sets the two side by side (1:1, 1:3). The remaining 12 occurrences (arḥām) mean the physical womb — even of animals (6:143-144) — or blood-relatives, with no mercy content, and the Qurʾan never derives the womb sense from mercy. So the honest result is one dominant, well-supported mercy sense PLUS one separate, unbridged womb/kinship class — hence a representative, moderately graded claim, not a universal one.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: The mercy nucleus does NOT entail: (a) forgiveness — irḥam is co-requested with but distinct from ighfir (23:109) and paired as ghafūrun raḥīm; (b) exemption from justice/punishment — direct antonymy with ʿadhāb (29:21:4:2, 17:54:6:1, 6:16:6:1), and even the name-holder decrees harm (36:23:7:2, 19:45:8:2); (c) harshness/severity — ruḥamāʾ set against ashiddāʾ (48:29:9:1); (d) something owed or universal — bestowed by will (man yashāʾ, 2:105:19:2) and contingent on obedience (passive turḥamūn); (e) mere sentiment — it is enacted relief (rain 30:50:4:1, deliverance 11:58:9:2, the Prophet 21:107:4:1). Separately, raḥīm (attribute) is NOT synonymous with al-Raḥmān (name) despite one gloss (juxtaposed 1:1, 1:3), and al-Raḥmān is God-exclusive whereas raḥīm is not (9:128:14:1). The concrete arḥām sense is NOT a divine attribute, never verbal/adjectival, and applies to animals — it lies OUTSIDE the disposition.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: At 6:143:17:1 and 6:144:15:1 arḥām denotes the physical WOMBS OF LIVESTOCK (sheep/goats/camels/cattle) inside a dietary-law polemic, and at 13:8:9:2 mā taghīḍu l-arḥām it is pure gestational physiology — zero compassion/benefaction content, and the Qurʾan supplies no internal derivation linking this concrete nominal to the mercy disposition. This defeats any single-meaning claim over all 339 tokens.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: A single unifying super-gloss 'enveloping, sheltering, life-giving care', with the WOMB as prototype and divine mercy as its extension (support: 3:6 juxtaposing yuṣawwirukum fi l-arḥām with the divine names; ruḥm at 18:81 for kin-tenderness; filial raḥmah at 17:24). REJECTED because it is not licensed Quran-internally: the text nowhere derives mercy from the womb; 3:6's adjacency is not predication and 18:81's ruḥm is affection, not the organ; the dominant mercy evidence carries zero kinship content (raḥmah = rain, revelation, deliverance) and the arḥām occurrences carry zero mercy content (13:8; 6:143-144). The super-gloss survives only by importing external etymology the source policy forbids and is so abstract (it must cover both a ewe's uterus and averted ʿadhāb) that it violates the narrowness mandate. The narrower two-class account is preferred.

internal_discovery.rationale: All three lenses independently converged: RAHIM 115 + RAHMA 114 + RAHMAN 57 + VERB 28 + RAHIMIN 6 + ARHAM-elative 4 + RUHM 1 + RUHAMA 1 + MARHAMA 1 = 327 dispositional occurrences forming ONE coherent, adversarially-clean mercy nucleus, PLUS ARHAM 12 forming a resistant, lexicalized concrete nominal (womb/blood-kinship). Per contract, a resistant lexicalized/nominal sub-class that the text does not bridge caps strength at MODERATE and scope at REPRESENTATIVE and forbids a UNIVERSAL single-gloss; the nucleus TAKEN ALONE is STRONG (broad, distinctive, opposed cleanly to ʿadhāb, attested horizontally as well as divinely). This is NOT chosen as UNRESOLVED because there is a clearly dominant, internally-demonstrated account (327/339) rather than two co-equal contesting senses; the minority arḥām class is honestly recorded as an unbridged resistant class rather than forced into unity. A secondary intra-nucleus lexicalization (al-Raḥmān as fossilized name, bleached in harm contexts 36:23/19:45) is an additional grade-capping datum but does not break the mercy sense.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Intensive attribute (faʿīl) 'ever-merciful/compassionate': a disposition to spare and benefit one in need.
clusters.classification_rationale: Reads as a shareable compassionate disposition throughout; sits beside retribution formulae (e.g. sarīʿu l-ʿiqāb ... ghafūrun raḥīm) yet always names the sparing/benefiting pole.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 115 occurrences, the habitual divine attribute, overwhelmingly clause-final in fixed doublets (ghafūrun raḥīm, ʿazīzun raḥīm, raʾūfun raḥīm). Reduces to the same spare-and-benefit relation as the verb and raḥmah, but is an ATTRIBUTE, not a name: unlike raḥmān it is predicable of a human (9:128, the Prophet), which the Qurʾan itself contrasts by pairing al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm (1:1, 1:3).

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Lexicalized quasi-proper divine name 'al-Raḥmān'; content is 'mercy' but functions as a reserved, God-exclusive name.
clusters.classification_rationale: Consistent as the mercy-name; its bleached compositionality in harm/punishment contexts is recorded as an adversarial boundary, not a counter-sense.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 57 occurrences, always definite, always God, never predicates a noun. Interchangeable with Allāh (17:110:6:2 ʾudʿū llāha aw ʾudʿū l-raḥmān), contested by deniers AS a name (25:60 wa-mā l-raḥmān). A lexicalized NAME, not a semantic split from raḥīm; the Qurʾan foregrounds the name-vs-attribute distinction at 1:1/1:3. Compositional force can be suspended in context (36:23:7:2 the Raḥmān may will harm; 19:45:8:2 ʿadhāb from the Raḥmān) — a grade-capping lexicalization datum, but sense stays 'mercy'.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: To show mercy = to spare from harm/punishment and bestow benefit (subject overwhelmingly God).
clusters.classification_rationale: Uniform spare-and-benefit act; the one human-directed token (17:24 irḥamhumā, to parents) still fits the same relation.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 28 occurrences. Two decisive collocations: mercy set AGAINST punishment (29:21:4:2 yuʿadhdhibu man yashāʾu wa-yarḥamu man yashāʾu; 17:54:6:1) and mercy as deliverance/removal of harm (6:16:6:1 faqad raḥimahu; 23:75). Passive turḥamūn is contingent on obedience/taqwā. Imperative irḥam always paired-with-but-distinct-from ighfir (23:109:11:2).

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Active participle plural 'those who show mercy'; God as the superlative among them.
clusters.classification_rationale: Consistent; agentive form of the same disposition.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 6 occurrences, fused in supplication anta arḥamu l-rāḥimīn (7:151:11:2 etc.) and khayru l-rāḥimīn (23:109:14:2). Same mercy relation, superlative frame.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Elative 'most merciful' — superlative of the same disposition.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 4 occurrences, all in the fixed du-ʿāʾ arḥamu l-rāḥimīn (7:151:10:1, 12:64:16:1, 12:92:10:1, 21:83:9:1).

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: ruḥm (18:81) — filial tenderness/mercy of a replacement child; dispositional, NOT the organ.
clusters.classification_rationale: Consistent with the mercy pole; flagged as the single token nearest a womb/mercy bridge, but it denotes affection, not the womb, so it does not license folding arḥām into the nucleus.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 1 occurrence, aqraba ruḥman. Semantically belongs to the mercy family (affection/mercy), not to the arḥām concrete nominal — so even the one lexeme nearest a bridge stays on the disposition side.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: ruḥamāʾ (48:29) — believers 'merciful among themselves'; enjoined horizontal compassion.
clusters.classification_rationale: Consistent; human interpersonal instance of the disposition, with a built-in negative boundary (vs shidda).
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 1 occurrence, ruḥamāʾu baynahum, explicitly opposed to ashiddāʾu ʿalā l-kuffār — mercy as directional, scoped, and set against harshness.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: marḥamah (90:17) — enjoined mutual compassion as a virtue.
clusters.classification_rationale: Consistent; enjoined-virtue instance of the disposition.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 1 occurrence, tawāṣaw bil-marḥamah (paired with ṣabr). Human-register nominal of the same mercy relation.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: arḥām — the physical gestational organ (incl. of livestock) and, by metonymy, blood-kinship; a lexicalized concrete nominal with NO dispositional/compassion content.
clusters.classification_rationale: Reads as a concrete organ / descent-bond in every occurrence; resists the mercy nucleus on Quran-internal grounds and is the resistant lexicalized sub-class that caps the root claim at MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 12 occurrences. Anatomical: 13:8:9:2 mā taghīḍu l-arḥām; 22:5:29:2 nuqirru fi l-arḥām; 3:6:5:2 yuṣawwirukum fi l-arḥām; 31:34:11:2; 2:228:15:1; and decisively of ANIMAL wombs 6:143:17:1 / 6:144:15:1 arḥāmu l-unthayayn. Blood-kinship: 4:1:23:3 wa-l-arḥām; 47:22:10:1 tuqaṭṭiʿū arḥāmakum; 33:6:9:2 & 8:75:11:2 ulū l-arḥām; 60:3:3:1. In none is mercy predicated of the arḥām; the Qurʾan never derives this sense from raḥmah and, where it wants kin-compassion, reaches for the mercy lexemes (17:24, 18:81, 48:29, 90:17), never arḥām. Morphologically inside the root, semantically unbridged.

reconciliation.rationale: mā taghīḍu l-arḥām is pure gestational physiology; no compassion reading is available and no Quran-internal derivation links it to raḥmah. Anchors the resistant class.
arḥāmu l-unthayayn = livestock wombs in a food-law dispute; a mercy abstraction reaching a ewe's uterus requires external etymology the source policy forbids. Confirms two unbridged classes.
Predication of the Prophet confirms raḥīm is a shareable attribute, sharpening the name(al-Raḥmān)-vs-attribute(raḥīm) distinction within the nucleus rather than resisting it.

ruḥm denotes filial affection (dispositional), not the organ; it stays in the mercy family and, being a hapax in an elliptical narrative, cannot carry a bridging claim — so it does not merge the poles.

adversarial_verification.notes: PASSED is withheld because an entire coherent sub-class (arḥām, 12 occ.) resists the mercy account and is Quran-internally unbridged; NOT_RUN is recorded (core holds, resistance logged) rather than FAILED because the dispositional nucleus itself is not refuted — its distinctiveness (opposition to ʿadhāb, distinctness from maghfira, directional enacted favor) survives every adversarial probe within the 327-token family.

occurrence_dispositions.note: Lexicalized concrete nominal (womb/blood-kinship); unbridged to the mercy nucleus.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: arḥām — the physical gestational organ (incl. of livestock) and, by metonymy, blood-kinship; a lexicalized concrete nominal with NO dispositional/compassion content.
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: 12 occurrences. Anatomical: 13:8:9:2 mā taghīḍu l-arḥām; 22:5:29:2 nuqirru fi l-arḥām; 3:6:5:2 yuṣawwirukum fi l-arḥām; 31:34:11:2; 2:228:15:1; and decisively of ANIMAL wombs 6:143:17:1 / 6:144:15:1 arḥāmu l-unthayayn. Blood-kinship: 4:1:23:3 wa-l-arḥām; 47:22:10:1 tuqaṭṭiʿū arḥāmakum; 33:6:9:2 & 8:75:11:2 ulū l-arḥām; 60:3:3:1. In none is mercy predicated of the arḥām; the Qurʾan never derives this sense from raḥmah and, where it wants kin-compassion, reaches for the mercy lexemes (17:24, 18:81, 48:29, 90:17), never arḥām. Morphologically inside the root, semantically unbridged.
occurrence_dispositions.preliminary_note: Same root rHm; tested whether the womb could be read as a metaphor of enveloping mercy.
occurrence_dispositions.reconciliation_rationale: mā taghīḍu l-arḥām is pure gestational physiology; no compassion reading is available and no Quran-internal derivation links it to raḥmah. Anchors the resistant class.

occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Intensive attribute (faʿīl) 'ever-merciful/compassionate': a disposition to spare and benefit one in need.
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: 115 occurrences, the habitual divine attribute, overwhelmingly clause-final in fixed doublets (ghafūrun raḥīm, ʿazīzun raḥīm, raʾūfun raḥīm). occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: 57 occurrences, always definite, always God, never predicates a noun. Interchangeable with Allāh (17:110:6:2 ʾudʿū llāha aw ʾudʿū l-raḥmān), contested by deniers AS a name (25:60 wa-mā l-raḥmān). occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: arḥām — the physical gestational organ (incl. of livestock) and, by metonymy, blood-kinship; a lexicalized concrete nominal with NO dispositional/compassion content.
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: 12 occurrences. Anatomical: 13:8:9:2 mā taghīḍu l-arḥām; 22:5:29:2 nuqirru fi l-arḥām; 3:6:5:2 yuṣawwirukum fi l-arḥām; 31:34:11:2; 2:228:15:1; and decisively of ANIMAL wombs 6:143:17:1 / 6:144:15:1 arḥāmu l-unthayayn. Blood-kinship: 4:1:23:3 wa-l-arḥām; 47:22:10:1 tuqaṭṭiʿū arḥāmakum; 33:6:9:2 & 8:75:11:2 ulū l-arḥām; 60:3:3:1. In none is mercy predicated of the arḥām; the Qurʾan never derives this sense from raḥmah and, where it wants kin-compassion, reaches for the mercy lexemes (17:24, 18:81, 48:29, 90:17), never arḥām. Morphologically inside the root, semantically unbridged.
occurrence_dispositions.preliminary_note: Same root rHm; tested whether the womb could be read as a metaphor of enveloping mercy.
verifier_objection: No Quran-internal predication of mercy on the arḥām; applies to animal wombs (6:143-144) and pure physiology (13:8); no gloss derives it from raḥmah.

Two decisive collocations: mercy set AGAINST punishment (29:21:4:2 yuʿadhdhibu man yashāʾu wa-yarḥamu man yashāʾu; 17:54:6:1) and mercy as deliverance/removal of harm (6:16:6:1 faqad raḥimahu; 23:75). Passive turḥamūn is contingent on obedience/taqwā. Imperative irḥam always paired-with-but-distinct-from ighfir (23:109:11:2).
occurrence_dispositions.preliminary_note: Uniform spare-and-benefit act; the one human-directed token (17:24 irḥamhumā, to parents) still fits the same relation.

occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: 57 occurrences, always definite, always God, never predicates a noun. occurrence_dispositions.note: Consistent as the mercy-name; its bleached compositionality in harm/punishment contexts is recorded as an adversarial boundary, not a counter-sense.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Lexicalized quasi-proper divine name 'al-Raḥmān'; content is 'mercy' but functions as a reserved, God-exclusive name.
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: 57 occurrences, always definite, always God, never predicates a noun. Interchangeable with Allāh (17:110:6:2 ʾudʿū llāha aw ʾudʿū l-raḥmān), contested by deniers AS a name (25:60 wa-mā l-raḥmān). A lexicalized NAME, not a semantic split from raḥīm; the Qurʾan foregrounds the name-vs-attribute distinction at 1:1/1:3. Compositional force can be suspended in context (36:23:7:2 the Raḥmān may will harm; 19:45:8:2 ʿadhāb from the Raḥmān) — a grade-capping lexicalization datum, but sense stays 'mercy'.
occurrence_dispositions.preliminary_note: Consistent as the mercy-name; its bleached compositionality in harm/punishment contexts is recorded as an adversarial boundary, not a counter-sense.

occurrence_dispositions.note: Lexicalized concrete nominal (womb/blood-kinship); unbridged to the mercy nucleus.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: arḥām — the physical gestational organ (incl. of livestock) and, by metonymy, blood-kinship; a lexicalized concrete nominal with NO dispositional/compassion content.
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: 12 occurrences. Anatomical: 13:8:9:2 mā taghīḍu l-arḥām; 22:5:29:2 nuqirru fi l-arḥām; 3:6:5:2 yuṣawwirukum fi l-arḥām; 31:34:11:2; 2:228:15:1; and decisively of ANIMAL wombs 6:143:17:1 / 6:144:15:1 arḥāmu l-unthayayn. Blood-kinship: 4:1:23:3 wa-l-arḥām; 47:22:10:1 tuqaṭṭiʿū arḥāmakum; 33:6:9:2 & 8:75:11:2 ulū l-arḥām; 60:3:3:1. In none is mercy predicated of the arḥām; the Qurʾan never derives this sense from raḥmah and, where it wants kin-compassion, reaches for the mercy lexemes (17:24, 18:81, 48:29, 90:17), never arḥām. Morphologically inside the root, semantically unbridged.
occurrence_dispositions.preliminary_note: Same root rHm; tested whether the womb could be read as a metaphor of enveloping mercy.
verifier_objection: No Quran-internal predication of mercy on the arḥām; applies to animal wombs (6:143-144) and pure physiology (13:8); no gloss derives it from raḥmah.

occurrence_dispositions.note: Lexicalized concrete nominal (womb/blood-kinship); unbridged to the mercy nucleus.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: arḥām — the physical gestational organ (incl. of livestock) and, by metonymy, blood-kinship; a lexicalized concrete nominal with NO dispositional/compassion content.
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: 12 occurrences. Anatomical: 13:8:9:2 mā taghīḍu l-arḥām; 22:5:29:2 nuqirru fi l-arḥām; 3:6:5:2 yuṣawwirukum fi l-arḥām; 31:34:11:2; 2:228:15:1; and decisively of ANIMAL wombs 6:143:17:1 / 6:144:15:1 arḥāmu l-unthayayn. Blood-kinship: 4:1:23:3 wa-l-arḥām; 47:22:10:1 tuqaṭṭiʿū arḥāmakum; 33:6:9:2 & 8:75:11:2 ulū l-arḥām; 60:3:3:1. In none is mercy predicated of the arḥām; the Qurʾan never derives this sense from raḥmah and, where it wants kin-compassion, reaches for the mercy lexemes (17:24, 18:81, 48:29, 90:17), never arḥām. Morphologically inside the root, semantically unbridged.
occurrence_dispositions.preliminary_note: Same root rHm; tested whether the womb could be read as a metaphor of enveloping mercy.
verifier_objection: No Quran-internal predication of mercy on the arḥām; applies to animal wombs (6:143-144) and pure physiology (13:8); no gloss derives it from raḥmah.

occurrence_dispositions.note: Lexicalized concrete nominal (womb/blood-kinship); unbridged to the mercy nucleus.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: arḥām — the physical gestational organ (incl. of livestock) and, by metonymy, blood-kinship; a lexicalized concrete nominal with NO dispositional/compassion content.
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: 12 occurrences. Anatomical: 13:8:9:2 mā taghīḍu l-arḥām; 22:5:29:2 nuqirru fi l-arḥām; 3:6:5:2 yuṣawwirukum fi l-arḥām; 31:34:11:2; 2:228:15:1; and decisively of ANIMAL wombs 6:143:17:1 / 6:144:15:1 arḥāmu l-unthayayn. Blood-kinship: 4:1:23:3 wa-l-arḥām; 47:22:10:1 tuqaṭṭiʿū arḥāmakum; 33:6:9:2 & 8:75:11:2 ulū l-arḥām; 60:3:3:1. In none is mercy predicated of the arḥām; the Qurʾan never derives this sense from raḥmah and, where it wants kin-compassion, reaches for the mercy lexemes (17:24, 18:81, 48:29, 90:17), never arḥām. Morphologically inside the root, semantically unbridged.
occurrence_dispositions.preliminary_note: Same root rHm; tested whether the womb could be read as a metaphor of enveloping mercy.
verifier_objection: No Quran-internal predication of mercy on the arḥām; applies to animal wombs (6:143-144) and pure physiology (13:8); no gloss derives it from raḥmah.

occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: The reified/enacted favor: the mercy that is bestowed — relief of harm, deliverance, rain/life, provision, revelation, the Prophet, reward.
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: 114 occurrences. The same disposition concretized into a dispensable good God alone controls and allots selectively (35:2:6:1 none can withhold; 2:105:19:2 yakhtaṣṣu bi-raḥmatihi man yashāʾ), the object of non-despair (39:53:10:1), self-imposed on God (6:54:13:2). Instantiated as deliverance (11:58:9:2), reviving rain (30:50:4:1), the Prophet (21:107:4:1); also human filial tenderness (17:24:6:2).

occurrence_dispositions.note: Consistent as the mercy-name; its bleached compositionality in harm/punishment contexts is recorded as an adversarial boundary, not a counter-sense.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Lexicalized quasi-proper divine name 'al-Raḥmān'; content is 'mercy' but functions as a reserved, God-exclusive name.
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: 57 occurrences, always definite, always God, never predicates a noun. Interchangeable with Allāh (17:110:6:2 ʾudʿū llāha aw ʾudʿū l-raḥmān), contested by deniers AS a name (25:60 wa-mā l-raḥmān). occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: To show mercy = to spare from harm/punishment and bestow benefit (subject overwhelmingly God).
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: 28 occurrences. occurrence_dispositions.note: Lexicalized concrete nominal (womb/blood-kinship); unbridged to the mercy nucleus.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: arḥām — the physical gestational organ (incl. of livestock) and, by metonymy, blood-kinship; a lexicalized concrete nominal with NO dispositional/compassion content.
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: 12 occurrences. Anatomical: 13:8:9:2 mā taghīḍu l-arḥām; 22:5:29:2 nuqirru fi l-arḥām; 3:6:5:2 yuṣawwirukum fi l-arḥām; 31:34:11:2; 2:228:15:1; and decisively of ANIMAL wombs 6:143:17:1 / 6:144:15:1 arḥāmu l-unthayayn. Blood-kinship: 4:1:23:3 wa-l-arḥām; 47:22:10:1 tuqaṭṭiʿū arḥāmakum; 33:6:9:2 & 8:75:11:2 ulū l-arḥām; 60:3:3:1. In none is mercy predicated of the arḥām; the Qurʾan never derives this sense from raḥmah and, where it wants kin-compassion, reaches for the mercy lexemes (17:24, 18:81, 48:29, 90:17), never arḥām. Morphologically inside the root, semantically unbridged.
occurrence_dispositions.preliminary_note: Same root rHm; tested whether the womb could be read as a metaphor of enveloping mercy.
verifier_objection: No Quran-internal predication of mercy on the arḥām; applies to animal wombs (6:143-144) and pure physiology (13:8); no gloss derives it from raḥmah.

Anatomical: 13:8:9:2 mā taghīḍu l-arḥām; 22:5:29:2 nuqirru fi l-arḥām; 3:6:5:2 yuṣawwirukum fi l-arḥām; 31:34:11:2; 2:228:15:1; and decisively of ANIMAL wombs 6:143:17:1 / 6:144:15:1 arḥāmu l-unthayayn. Blood-kinship: 4:1:23:3 wa-l-arḥām; 47:22:10:1 tuqaṭṭiʿū arḥāmakum; 33:6:9:2 & 8:75:11:2 ulū l-arḥām; 60:3:3:1. In none is mercy predicated of the arḥām; the Qurʾan never derives this sense from raḥmah and, where it wants kin-compassion, reaches for the mercy lexemes (17:24, 18:81, 48:29, 90:17), never arḥām. Morphologically inside the root, semantically unbridged.

occurrence_dispositions.note: Lexicalized concrete nominal (womb/blood-kinship); unbridged to the mercy nucleus.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: arḥām — the physical gestational organ (incl. of livestock) and, by metonymy, blood-kinship; a lexicalized concrete nominal with NO dispositional/compassion content.
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: 12 occurrences. Anatomical: 13:8:9:2 mā taghīḍu l-arḥām; 22:5:29:2 nuqirru fi l-arḥām; 3:6:5:2 yuṣawwirukum fi l-arḥām; 31:34:11:2; 2:228:15:1; and decisively of ANIMAL wombs 6:143:17:1 / 6:144:15:1 arḥāmu l-unthayayn. Blood-kinship: 4:1:23:3 wa-l-arḥām; 47:22:10:1 tuqaṭṭiʿū arḥāmakum; 33:6:9:2 & 8:75:11:2 ulū l-arḥām; 60:3:3:1. In none is mercy predicated of the arḥām; the Qurʾan never derives this sense from raḥmah and, where it wants kin-compassion, reaches for the mercy lexemes (17:24, 18:81, 48:29, 90:17), never arḥām. Morphologically inside the root, semantically unbridged.
occurrence_dispositions.preliminary_note: Same root rHm; tested whether the womb could be read as a metaphor of enveloping mercy.
verifier_objection: No Quran-internal predication of mercy on the arḥām; applies to animal wombs (6:143-144) and pure physiology (13:8); no gloss derives it from raḥmah.

occurrence_dispositions.note: Lexicalized concrete nominal (womb/blood-kinship); unbridged to the mercy nucleus.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: arḥām — the physical gestational organ (incl. of livestock) and, by metonymy, blood-kinship; a lexicalized concrete nominal with NO dispositional/compassion content.
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: 12 occurrences. Anatomical: 13:8:9:2 mā taghīḍu l-arḥām; 22:5:29:2 nuqirru fi l-arḥām; 3:6:5:2 yuṣawwirukum fi l-arḥām; 31:34:11:2; 2:228:15:1; and decisively of ANIMAL wombs 6:143:17:1 / 6:144:15:1 arḥāmu l-unthayayn. Blood-kinship: 4:1:23:3 wa-l-arḥām; 47:22:10:1 tuqaṭṭiʿū arḥāmakum; 33:6:9:2 & 8:75:11:2 ulū l-arḥām; 60:3:3:1. In none is mercy predicated of the arḥām; the Qurʾan never derives this sense from raḥmah and, where it wants kin-compassion, reaches for the mercy lexemes (17:24, 18:81, 48:29, 90:17), never arḥām. Morphologically inside the root, semantically unbridged.
occurrence_dispositions.preliminary_note: Same root rHm; tested whether the womb could be read as a metaphor of enveloping mercy.
verifier_objection: No Quran-internal predication of mercy on the arḥām; applies to animal wombs (6:143-144) and pure physiology (13:8); no gloss derives it from raḥmah.

occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: 57 occurrences, always definite, always God, never predicates a noun. Interchangeable with Allāh (17:110:6:2 ʾudʿū llāha aw ʾudʿū l-raḥmān), contested by deniers AS a name (25:60 wa-mā l-raḥmān). A lexicalized NAME, not a semantic split from raḥīm; the Qurʾan foregrounds the name-vs-attribute distinction at 1:1/1:3. Compositional force can be suspended in context (36:23:7:2 the Raḥmān may will harm; 19:45:8:2 ʿadhāb from the Raḥmān) — a grade-capping lexicalization datum, but sense stays 'mercy'.

occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Lexicalized quasi-proper divine name 'al-Raḥmān'; content is 'mercy' but functions as a reserved, God-exclusive name.
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: 57 occurrences, always definite, always God, never predicates a noun. Interchangeable with Allāh (17:110:6:2 ʾudʿū llāha aw ʾudʿū l-raḥmān), contested by deniers AS a name (25:60 wa-mā l-raḥmān). A lexicalized NAME, not a semantic split from raḥīm; the Qurʾan foregrounds the name-vs-attribute distinction at 1:1/1:3. Compositional force can be suspended in context (36:23:7:2 the Raḥmān may will harm; 19:45:8:2 ʿadhāb from the Raḥmān) — a grade-capping lexicalization datum, but sense stays 'mercy'.
occurrence_dispositions.preliminary_note: Consistent as the mercy-name; its bleached compositionality in harm/punishment contexts is recorded as an adversarial boundary, not a counter-sense.

candidate_root_contribution: Across the dispositional derivational family (~327 of 339 occ.: verb, raḥmah, raḥīm, al-Raḥmān, rāḥimīn, arḥam, ruḥm, ruḥamāʾ, marḥamah) rHm contributes a BENEFICENT SPARING FAVOR extended by a superior/agent toward one in need or weakness — inclining to spare from harm/punishment and to bestow benefit. It is relational and directional (God→creature, or strong→weak), enacted rather than merely felt (instantiated as deliverance, reviving rain, provision, revelation, the Prophet, reward), discretionary/contingent (bestowed man yashāʾ, conditioned on taqwā), and defined by the corpus as the pole OPPOSITE to punishment (ʿadhāb) and distinct from forgiveness (maghfira). This account is NOT extended to the concrete nominal arḥām (womb/blood-kinship, 12 occ.), which the Qurʾan never bridges to the disposition.

layer_attribution.occurrence_evidence: Direct token facts: mercy set against ʿadhāb (29:21:4:2, 17:54:6:1), mercy as deliverance (6:16:6:1, 11:58:9:2), irḥam co-requested with ighfir (23:109), passive turḥamūn contingent on taqwā, and arḥām as womb/livestock/kinship (13:8:9:2, 6:143:17:1, 47:22:10:1).
layer_attribution.derivation: Ten derivational lexemes of rHm: raḥīm(115), raḥmah(114), raḥmān(57), verb(28), rāḥimīn(6), arḥam-elative(4), ruḥm(1), ruḥamāʾ(1), marḥamah(1) — nine dispositional — versus arḥām(12), pl. of raḥim, the concrete nominal. Nine of ten derivations carry the disposition; one does not.
layer_attribution.lexical_class: Two lexicalizations recorded: al-Raḥmān as a fossilized God-exclusive proper NAME (compositionally bleached in 36:23/19:45) vs raḥīm as a shareable ATTRIBUTE (9:128); and arḥām as a lexicalized concrete nominal (womb/blood-kinship) standing outside the mercy sense.
layer_attribution.contextual_relation: Referential/contextual instantiations of raḥmah — reviving rain (30:50:4:1), revelation/guidance, the Prophet (21:107:4:1), provision, paradise — are CONTEXTUAL realizations of the one favor-relation and must NOT be promoted into the root claim; the root contributes the sparing-favor relation, not 'rain' or 'the Book'.
layer_attribution.reconciliation: Preliminary STRUCTURAL_UNCERTAINTY on arḥām (tested as possible enveloping-mercy metaphor) was resolved to RESISTANT on Quran-internal grounds (animal wombs, pure physiology, no derivation from raḥmah); 9:128 and 18:81 were resolved to CONSISTENT within the nucleus (attribute-sharing; affection not organ).
layer_attribution.unresolved_resistance: The arḥām class (12 occ.: 13:8:9:2, 22:5:29:2, 2:228:15:1, 31:34:11:2, 33:6:9:2, 3:6:5:2, 47:22:10:1, 4:1:23:3, 60:3:3:1, 6:143:17:1, 6:144:15:1, 8:75:11:2) remains an unbridged resistant sub-class; the womb→mercy link asserted by the competing super-gloss is not Quran-internally demonstrated.

evidence_basis.statement: al-Raḥmān appears with harm/punishment (36:23 bi-ḍurr; 19:45 ʿadhāb min al-raḥmān), showing the name is lexicalized and its compositional 'mercy' force can be contextually suspended while its sense remains 'mercy'.

hard_case_representation.rationale: The 12 arḥām occurrences persist as a resistant, Quran-internally unbridged concrete nominal class (womb/blood-kinship) and are recorded as RESISTANT_SEAM hard cases and as counterevidence. Additional adversarial-boundary and structural-atypicality hard cases (al-Raḥmān willing harm 36:23; raḥīm of the Prophet 9:128; the near-bridge ruḥm 18:81) are recorded but do not overturn the dominant mercy nucleus — hence PERSISTED_RESISTANCE_OR_ADVERSARIAL rather than a clean falsification.

rejection_condition.challenging_finding: A Quran-internal occurrence in which the arḥām (womb/blood-kinship) class is itself predicated with mercy/benefaction, OR in which the text explicitly derives raḥmah from the womb — which would collapse the two-class partition into a single nucleus and force the representative claim upward toward root-general.
rejection_condition.search_location: The 12 arḥām occurrences (13:8:9:2, 22:5:29:2, 2:228:15:1, 31:34:11:2, 33:6:9:2, 3:6:5:2, 47:22:10:1, 4:1:23:3, 60:3:3:1, 6:143:17:1, 6:144:15:1, 8:75:11:2) and any verse co-locating arḥām with a rHm mercy-lexeme; plus the bridge candidate ruḥm 18:81:9:1.
rejection_condition.verification_method: Read each arḥām occurrence for a predicate ascribing compassion/sparing/benefaction TO the arḥām, or an explicit gloss equating arḥām with raḥmah; confirm via qac_pos/morphology that the token is the concrete nominal and check the full verse_text for the linking predication.
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Reject mere lexical co-occurrence, external etymology, translation glosses, or thematic adjacency (as at 3:6) as evidence of a bridge; require an actual Quran-internal predication, not proximity. Also exclude ruḥm/marḥamah (dispositional, already in the nucleus) from counting as arḥām.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If no such internal bridge is found, the two-class partition stands and the claim remains REPRESENTATIVE/MODERATE; if a genuine bridge is found, merge the classes and re-evaluate toward ROOT_GENERALIZATION, or if the bridge is contested, downgrade to UNRESOLVED.

reopen_conditions: Reopen if any occurrence predicates mercy/sparing/benefaction directly of the arḥām, or if the Qurʾan is found to gloss arḥām by raḥmah — collapsing the womb/kinship class into the mercy nucleus.

Reopen the name-vs-attribute split if al-Raḥmān is ever found predicated of a human or used as a common (non-referential) adjective, or if raḥīm is found to be as God-exclusive as al-Raḥmān (contra 9:128).
Reopen the two-pole partition if ruḥm (18:81) or a further token is shown to bridge filial kinship-affection to the physical womb organ, licensing a single enveloping-care nucleus.
Reopen if the al-Raḥmān-with-harm data (36:23, 19:45) is shown to shift the name's sense away from mercy rather than merely bleach its compositionality.

falsification_evidence.status_rationale: PASSED is withheld because an entire coherent sub-class (arḥām, 12 occ.) resists the mercy account and is Quran-internally unbridged; NOT_RUN is recorded (core holds, resistance logged) rather than FAILED because the dispositional nucleus itself is not refuted — its distinctiveness (opposition to ʿadhāb, distinctness from maghfira, directional enacted favor) survives every adversarial probe within the 327-token family.
